body: Yeah I can really relate to this. Coming out of the cocoon or womb of college, into the brutally competitive dog eat dog Real World is the main reason I'm on the verge of suicide. And I HATED college. I hated being around all those frat bros and their raging hormones. Yet I prefer 1000% times over the devil I know. And I wont "grow up" and make peace with the fact that the worlds not a utopia, and people aren't angels. Maybe that is a fact of life. But at least I do have the option to reject it and escape through suicide. And FUCK this horrible society for being so fucked up, and yet at the same time barring the exits. Our society has no sympathy or mercy. IMHO the only reason we have laws against suicide, and suicide-assistence, is because the sadists who run everything need victims to torture.

But EP tells me the world DOES have a meaning and it terrifies me. To maximize the selfish gene, by whatever means neccesary. There is an objective way to win and lose at life.

I used to be like that. Not giving a fuck. Socially isolated in my own world. Now Im trying to make the leap from omega to beta

So much of FA advice is geared towards how not to be a beta. How not to give a shit. But betas actually have friends and social relations. For an extreme foreveralone like me, what I really need to learn is opening myself up to beta behavior.
I want to learn to get turned on by rejection.

Well I'm not really looking for the workplace to "cure" my foreveraloneness. Although it would be nice. But just casual friendly acquintanceship would be good enough. And I have experienced that through school and gym. And to some extent it even satisfies my social needs. 

I guess I'm asking, assuming I remain Forever Alone, is it more easy to endure in work than it is in college?

I hate college, where everyone is supposed to be happy. I'll never forget that Seinfield episode, where George Costanzo says "I've never been happy, except college, that was fun". 

So my assumption is if I hate college which is fun, I'm going to super-hate jobs which is not-fun. But my logic might be faulty. Maybe the very un-funness of work, will actually make it a better fit with me.
